solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Secret clique led by Democrat in China? (6,3)

indicators.note: whatever is led by something has that thing walking at its front, so D comes first

blocks.note: inner = private, secret, as in inner thoughts

annotation.surface: A secretive political faction run by a Democrat operating in China.
annotation.walkthrough: China is capitalised only because it opens the sentence's last phrase; the question mark warns that it means crockery, not the country.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a dinner set is a matching service of plates and dishes, typically made of china.

clue.text: Her son goes crazy with daughter ahead in polls (7)

indicators.note: letters that go crazy lose their sane order and are rearranged
something ahead is out in front, so the D leads the rearranged letters

annotation.surface: A mother's son behaves wildly while his sister leads in the opinion polls.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Polls' looks like elections, but to poll cattle is a farming term for cutting off their horns.
annotation.definitionFit: A farming sense: to poll cattle is to remove their horns, the same job as dehorning.

indicators.note: letters banned at regular intervals means every other one is thrown out

blocks.note: the even letters of aNd OrGy

annotation.surface: Drink and debauchery are both prohibited by some regular rule.
annotation.walkthrough: 'And' looks like a link word but is part of the letter string: the kept letters run across both words.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: nog is a strong ale from East Anglia, and also short for eggnog.

indicators.note: a building that houses something holds it inside, so the estate holds I'M

blocks.note: a manor is a landed estate
one is = I am, contracted to I'm

annotation.surface: A question of what someone's manor house is worth.
annotation.walkthrough: 'One's' reads as possessive, but here it is 'one is': the speaker is the one, so I AM, shortened to I'M.
annotation.definitionFit: Both are verbs of appraisal: to value a house is to put a figure on its worth.

annotation.surface: A complaint that there is little time for studying.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads the whole clue as one complaint about a short revision period; in fact 'Not much' is the definition and the rest is the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, used before a noun: scant attention is not much attention.

clue.text: Sign for staff meaning break cut short (5,4)

indicators.note: a word cut short has had its tail lopped off

blocks.note: the tenor of a remark is its gist or meaning
CLEFT, a break or split, cut short

annotation.surface: A notice for employees announcing that their break is being shortened.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Staff' looks like the workforce; it is the musical stave, and the clef is the sign at its start.
annotation.definitionFit: A musical sense: the tenor clef is the symbol written on a staff to fix the pitch of its lines.

clue.text: Old lady on organ is hot stuff (5)

indicators.note: in an across clue, something sitting on another thing comes after it

blocks.note: an organ is a publication, a magazine or mag
one's old lady = one's mother, ma

annotation.surface: An elderly woman at the church organ is a sensation.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Organ' suggests music or anatomy; it is a periodical, as in 'the party organ'.
annotation.definitionFit: A literal reading of a slang phrase: magma is molten rock, stuff that really is hot.

clue.text: Dog biting American man’s backside for sport (6)

indicators.note: a dog biting something has it between its jaws, so MUTT closes around the rest

annotation.surface: A dog playfully nips an American man's rear end.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sport' is the biologist's word for an organism that differs suddenly from its parents, not a game.
annotation.definitionFit: A biological sense: a sport is an offspring showing a sudden inherited variation, which is what a mutant is.

clue.text: Force poor navigator to adopt new way of processing data (11)

indicators.note: a poor navigator's letters are in poor shape, so they are rearranged
to adopt a child is to take it in, so the rearranged letters take IT inside

annotation.surface: A bad navigator being made to take up computer technology.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface puts 'poor' with 'navigator' as a description; it is the instruction to shuffle, and IT slots in after the fourth letter.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: gravitation is one of the fundamental forces of physics.

indicators.note: one thing after another comes later in the line, so FRONT follows A and F

blocks.note: F is foxtrot in the phonetic alphabet

annotation.surface: A touch of swagger after dancing a superb foxtrot.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Slight' reads as an adjective meaning small, but it is the noun meaning an insult.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym once 'slight' is read as a noun: a snub or insult to someone's dignity.

blocks.note: surface: a verb, someone having a meal; meant: the slang noun for food
when that food is served: late in the day

annotation.walkthrough: 'Eats' looks like a verb, someone dining; it is the slang noun for food. High tea is a British early-evening meal of cooked food with tea.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by description: the meal taken late in the afternoon, with cooked dishes as well as cake.

blocks.note: an emphatic yes, in British slang
taken literally: the half is negated, switched off

annotation.surface: An emphatic assurance that the sale really is half price.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Not half!' is British slang for an enthusiastic yes; the second reading takes the phrase literally.
annotation.definitionFit: A British idiom: 'Did you enjoy it?' 'Not half!' means definitely; literally, a half is not there.

indicators.note: something covered in sheets is wrapped inside them

blocks.note: a ream is 500 sheets of paper

annotation.surface: A stretch of ground left blanketed under sheets.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sheets' suggests bedding or rain; it is paper, counted in reams.
annotation.definitionFit: Area in the figurative sense, a field of interest, as in 'the realm of science'.

indicators.note: naughty letters misbehave and will not stay in order

annotation.surface: A wayward girl who is crazy about sherry.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Mad' looks like a second anagram signal, but it is fodder; 'Naughty' does the stirring.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: amontillado is a medium-dry style of Spanish sherry.

clue.text: He directs opening of Titanic, remade on a train (9)

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter
a film remade is made again differently, so the letters are rebuilt in a new order

annotation.surface: A film director reshoots the start of Titanic set on a train.
annotation.walkthrough: The film-making surface points at James Cameron, but the director wanted is Quentin Tarantino.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Quentin Tarantino is a film director, so he directs.

annotation.surface: A Broadway show's run was cut short, leaving money owed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Season on Broadway' suggests a theatre run; it is simply the American word for autumn.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym from accounting: the amount by which money falls short of what is needed.

clue.text: British leaving African capital, lost and in distress (9)

indicators.note: someone leaving a place is no longer in it, so B departs from the capital's name

blocks.note: to shed weight is to lose it

annotation.surface: A British expatriate leaves an African capital, lost and upset.
annotation.walkthrough: Bangui is the capital of the Central African Republic. 'Lost' looks like part of the traveller's plight but is its own piece.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: anguished describes someone suffering great mental distress.

indicators.note: the beast's last is its final letter

blocks.note: to savage a show is to pan it

annotation.surface: A wild animal's dying breath.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Savage beast' reads as one phrase; 'Savage' is a verb meaning to criticise harshly.
annotation.definitionFit: Both verbs describe short, laboured breathing.

clue.text: Wool caught on tree by lake (8)

indicators.note: in a down clue, a thing on another sits above it, so C tops ASH
something by the tree stands next to it, so MERE follows

annotation.surface: A tuft of fleece snagged on a lakeside tree.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Caught' is not the wool snagging but the cricket scorer's c; 'mere' is an old word common in English place names.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: cashmere is the fine wool of the Kashmir goat.

clue.text: See you in transit at airport (2-2)

indicators.note: the answer sits in the words that follow, straddling them

annotation.surface: A goodbye said to someone passing through an airport.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer runs across three words, which is why 'at' looks like innocent filler.
annotation.definitionFit: Both are casual British farewells.

clue.text: Understood issue coming up in the past (4,3)

indicators.note: in a down clue, something coming up travels upwards, so it reads bottom to top

blocks.note: 'I see' means I understand, so saw = understood

annotation.surface: A matter that was grasped when it came up earlier.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Issue' reads as a topic under discussion, and 'coming up' as it arising; both words are doing mechanical work, and the reversal takes in the whole string, not just the second part.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: 'time was when...' means there was a time, in the past, when.

blocks.note: bull and guff both mean nonsense

annotation.surface: A bull that is both impressive and hilarious.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bull' is not an animal but nonsense; 'inspiring' looks like a container instruction but is part of the phrase for AWING.
annotation.definitionFit: The answer as a verbal noun: a loud, hearty kind of laughter.

indicators.note: letters cycling go round like a wheel, the front one coming round to the back
one thing in another sits inside it, so the result goes inside the valley

blocks.note: DAD with its D moved to the back

annotation.surface: Encouraging a father out on a bike ride through a valley.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cycling' looks like a bike ride; here it rotates the letters of DAD. A glen is a Scottish valley.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym as a verb: to cheer someone up is to make them glad.

blocks.note: an ism is a doctrine or teaching

annotation.surface: A department of a school's teaching staff.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Division' reads as a school department; it is a split, especially within a church.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a split within a group into opposing factions, classically a church.

clue.text: Guy charged with current murder is copper’s source (9)

indicators.note: a gun charged with powder is loaded with it, so the guy is filled with the other letters

blocks.note: a hit is a contract killing

annotation.surface: A man accused of a recent killing turns out to be a police officer's informant.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like police slang, and 'source' an informant; here copper is the metal and its source an ore.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by description: malachite is a green mineral mined as an ore of copper.

indicators.note: the celebrity's second is the letter in second place

annotation.surface: A star's backup private plane.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Jet' is not a plane but the deep black colour, and 'second spare' is not a backup.
annotation.definitionFit: Both are names for a deep, glossy black, from the mineral and the wood.

indicators.note: without bounds means without the letters at its edges

blocks.note: Madras is now officially called Chennai
CHENNAI without its first and last letters

annotation.surface: The limitless colours of present-day Madras.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Modern' is the key: the city was renamed from Madras in 1996, and only the new name contains the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: A dye used as a colour: henna gives hair and skin a reddish-brown tint.

clue.text: Rather frail married couple welcoming each brief kiss (7)

indicators.note: a couple welcoming guests take them in, so W and H surround the rest
a brief kiss is cut short, losing its last letter

blocks.note: KISS with its last letter deleted, as 'brief' instructs

annotation.surface: An elderly married pair greeting each other with a quick peck.
annotation.walkthrough: W and H are the standard abbreviations for wife and husband, so they make the married couple.
annotation.definitionFit: The -ish suffix gives 'rather': weakish is somewhat weak, rather frail.

clue.text: Half-blind from love, yet endlessly in distress (3-4)

indicators.note: a word without its end has lost its last letter
one thing in another sits inside it

annotation.surface: Blinded by love and still desperate: a lovesick lament.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In distress' looks like one phrase meaning upset, which tempts a solver to hunt for an anagram; 'in' is a placement instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: A playful definition: with one eye you have half your sight, so half-blind.

indicators.note: something read aloud is heard, not seen, so the letter's spoken name counts

blocks.note: the 21st letter's spoken name is also a common pronoun

annotation.surface: A single letter being read out.
annotation.walkthrough: 'One' is the impersonal pronoun, as in 'one never knows', for which 'you' is the everyday substitute.
annotation.definitionFit: The generic pronoun: 'you never know' says the same as 'one never knows'.

clue.text: Charge round room after case of stout (5)

indicators.note: what comes after follows in the line, so round and room come behind ST
a word's case is its outer shell, its first and last letters

annotation.surface: A fee for delivering a crate of stout round to someone's room.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Case of stout' suggests a crate of beer; it means the outside letters of the word. 'Charge' is an attack, not a fee.
annotation.definitionFit: A military sense: to storm a position is to rush at and attack it.

indicators.note: pickled means drunk, so the letters stagger into a new order

annotation.surface: A menu offering pickled nuts: dull food.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fare' looks like food, fitting the pickled nut; it is a ticket price. A day return is a British rail ticket out and back on the same day.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: a day return is one kind of ticket price charged by British railways.
